<text:style bold="true">Actions</text:style>

<image:base64 col="0" width="44" wrap="none"></image:base64>

The Actions panel changes or builds on the objects that already exist. Some buttons
are active only when the selection is suitable: for each of them it is said below
when it is active, and otherwise it is grayed. Trim, Extend, Break and Mirror
are always active, because they ask for the objects after the button is pressed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Trim</text:style>
Click the part of a line between two crossings to hide it. Shift+click
restores the object. Nothing is deleted: the hidden part can always be
       brought back.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Extend</text:style>
Click near the end of a line or poly-line to prolong it up to the next
object. Shift+click removes the extension.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Break</text:style>
Click a first point on an object and then a second one: the part between them
is hidden. Shift+click restores the object.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Offset</text:style>
Select lines, poly-lines, polygons, rectangles, ellipses or arcs, press the
button and give the distance: a parallel copy is made, and it follows the
       original when this changes. For closed shapes a positive value goes towards
       the inside and a negative one towards the outside; the +/- button in the
       window changes the sign.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> at least one line, poly-line, polygon,
       rectangle, ellipse or arc is selected; otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Mirror</text:style>
Pick the objects (or select them first, Shift+click for more), then click the
axis line: the mirrored copy follows the original.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Fillet</text:style>
Select two straight lines that are joined at a point, or two following sides
of a polygon or poly-line, press the button and give the radius: the corner
       becomes a rounded one. For lines the arc follows them (its radius can be
       changed with the handle in the middle of the arc); for the sides of a polygon
       the corner is replaced by short sides.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> exactly two straight
       lines joined at a point are selected, or exactly two following sides of one
       polygon or poly-line (select the first side, then Shift+click the second);
       otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Chamfer</text:style>
The same as the fillet, but the corner is cut with a straight side: you give
the two distances from the corner.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> the same as the Fillet: two
       straight lines joined at a point, or two following sides of a polygon or
       poly-line.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Array</text:style>
Select the objects first, then press the button: it makes rectangular or
polar copies that follow the original.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> at least one object is
       selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Rotate</text:style>
Select the objects, press the button, give the angle and click the centre of
rotation.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> at least one object is selected (not the arc of a
       fillet or the cut of a chamfer, which follow their lines).

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Scale</text:style>
Select the objects, press the button and give the factor: they are scaled
around the centre of the selection.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> at least one object is
       selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Add joint</text:style>
Click a line, or a side of a poly-line or polygon, to add a vertex there. A
straight line becomes a poly-line.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a line, a poly-line or a
       polygon is selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Join</text:style>
The selected line, arrow, poly-line, polygon or spline shows its points. Click the point that must
move and then the point it must reach (on the same figure or on another one):
the first point goes onto the second one and the two become a single point,
kept together by a coincidence constraint. Only the figure of the first point
changes; the other one stays where it is.
       Splines are different: when the first point is an end of a spline and the
       second one is an end of another spline, the two become a single spline
       that goes on smoothly through the joint (no corner). When both points are the
       two ends of the same spline, the spline is closed in the same way.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> a line, an arrow, a poly-line, a polygon or a spline
is selected (it stays active while Join is in use). If the figure of the first point
is fixed, or the join contradicts the other constraints, nothing is changed and
a message tells why.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Add point to path</text:style>
Select a path, then click a point of it to add a new control point there.<text:style bold="true"></text:style>
<text:style bold="true">Active when:</text:style> a spline is selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Group</text:style>
Joins the selected objects into one that moves and resizes as a whole
(Ctrl+G).<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style> two or more objects are selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Ungroup</text:style>
Splits the selected groups into their elements (Ctrl+Shift+G).<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style>
at least one of the selected objects belongs to a group.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Merge rasters</text:style>
Select two rasters: they become one, as large as needed to hold both.<text:style bold="true"> Active</text:style>
<text:style bold="true">when:</text:style> exactly two raster pictures are selected.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Flip</text:style>
Turns the selected raster pictures upside down, and the selected groups too, as if
they were seen in a mirror under them (the axis is horizontal and goes through the centre
of each picture or of the box of each group). A group is not changed piece by piece: it
is turned over as a whole, and text keeps its letters the right way up.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style>
       every selected object is a raster picture or belongs to a group; otherwise it is grayed.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Mirror (left and right)</text:style>
Swaps left and right in the selected raster pictures and groups, about a vertical axis
through the centre of each picture or of the box of each group. It is not the Mirror
button of this panel that makes a copy about an axis line.<text:style bold="true"> Active when:</text:style>
       every selected object is a raster picture or belongs to a group; otherwise it is grayed.
